A.why: Gold spiked crown plus flared black pauldrons with molten strips: the clearest regal silhouette, reads from the ARPG camera, palette right.
A.fix: Thin the crown to fewer tines with a molten gem at its base; add a hip plate over the olive waist gap; widen the chest crack.

B.why: Molten plume and chest core gem, restrained Neon, but the outline is a black box from above.
B.fix: Taller swept flame crest; seat the gem in a raised socket; hip plate; a seam on the back.

C.why: Horned helm with glowing eyes and molten diamond heart; most distinctive outline from front and back, horns weaker from ARPG.
C.fix: Angle and thicken horns to read from above; frame the diamond; hip plate.

D.why: Vent-post pauldrons read well from above and suit the zone, but Neon and gold are overspent.
D.fix: Cut Neon to vent caps and one seam; cut gold trim; fewer, bigger vents; hip plate.

E.why: Thin gold spike crown vanishes from the high camera; orange pauldron strips dominate.
E.fix: Thicker, fewer crown spikes; tone pauldron strips; bigger chest crack; hip plate.

F.why: No silhouette idea that reads from above; a dark blob with one chest crack.
F.fix: Commit to one silhouette idea; run the crack up through the helm; molten seams on pauldron tops.

notes: All six share a waist gap where the olive avatar legs show between chest and boots; a hip plate fixes it on every set. A and C carry the strongest single ideas (crown, horns); C's horns need to survive the ARPG camera. D's vent posts are a good zone tie but overspend Neon.
